DRP-5335-05.description: It remains to be whether the cytostatic effect is entirely dependent on the alkylation of DNA or other mechanisms unknown that , such as inhibition of chromatin transformation processes or inhibition of DNA polymerases play a role. The metabolite acrolein , has no antineoplastic activity, but is responsible for the adverse urotoxic effect. Pharmacodynami :cs Used in the treatment of various forms of malignancies such as Burkitt’s and other non-Hodgkin’s lymphomas, multiple myeloma and mycosis fungoides. It is also used in gestational trophoblastic tumours and malignancies of the brain, breast, endometrium, lung, and ovary; in childhood malignancies such as neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma, Wilms’ tumour and in sarcomas and some leukemias. It is also indicated for the treatment of immune-mediated conditions such as severe rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupu erythematosus, vasculitis, dermatomyositis, and lung disease.s interstitial Cyclophosphamide is activated in the liver to the active metabolites 4-hydroxy-cyclophosphamide and aldofosfamide (tautomeric form of 4-hydroxy-cyclophosphamide) through phase I metabolism by cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes. Different CYP isozymes contribute to the bioactivation of Cyclophosphamide, including CYP2A6, 2B6, 2C9, 2C19 and 3A4, 2B6 in which it exhibits highest 4-hydroxylase activity. Detoxification is done mainly through glutathione-S-transferases (GSTA1, GSTP1) and alcohol dehydrogenase (ALDH1, ALDH3). Two to four hours after administration of yclophosphamide, the plasma C concentrations of the active metabolites are maximal, after which a rapid decrease of plasma concentrations takes place. Cyclophosphamide has been demonstrated to have a cytostatic effect in many tumour types. Cyclophosphamide is quickly and almost completely absorbed from parenteral sites. Distribution: The plasma half-life of yclophosphamide is about 4 to 8 hours in adults and children. The plasma half-lives of the active C metabolites are not known. Cross-resistance, especially with structurally related cytotoxic agents, e.g., ifosfamide, as well as other alkylating agents, cannot be excluded. Absorption: Cyclophosphamide engages probably to the S-or G2-phase of the cell cycle. Metabolism: Following high-dose IV administration within the framework of allogeneic bone marrow transplantation, the plasma concentration of pure yclophosphamide follows linear first-order kinetics. Compared with conventional yclophosphamide C C therapy, there is an increase in inactive metabolites, indicating saturation of activating enzyme systems, but not of the stages of metabolism leading to inactive metabolites. During the course of high-dose yclophosphamide therapy over several days, C there is a decrease in the areas under the plasma concentration-time curve of the parent compound, probably due to auto- induction of microsomal metabolism activity.
DRP-5335-05.indications: Initial treatment is given by intravenous injection. After satisfactory remission has occurred, maintenance therapy with tablets is recommended. Individual dosage should take into account the general state of the patient and the white blood count. PHARMACOKINETIC :S Less than 20% of yclophosphamide is bound to plasma proteins. The protein binding of the metabolites of yclophosphamide C C is higher but less than 70%. To what extent the active metabolites protein bound, is not known. Use During Lactation: Cyclophosphamide is excreted in breast milk. Therefore, nursing should be discontinued while the patient is on Cyclophosphamide therapy. Cyclophosphamide is administered as an inactive prodrug that is activated in the liver. Use During Pregnancy: Cyclophosphamide can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Therefore, if this drug is used during pregnancy, or if the patient becomes pregnant while taking this drug, the patient should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus. Women of child bearing potential should be advised to avoid pregnancy during Cyclophosphamide therapy.

DRP-5457.description: Tramadol Hydrochloride is readily absorbed following oral administration. Oral bioavailability is approximately 68% after a single dose and increases to 90% at steady state. Onset of action is dose dependent but generally occurs within an hour of dosing, peaking within 2 to 3 hours. Duration of analgesia is about 6 hours. The rate or extent of absorption is not significantly affected by co-administration with food. The bioavailability of Tramadol Hydrochloride after intramuscular injection or intravenous administration is the same; the mean peak serum concentration is achieved after 45 minutes. Tramadol Hydrochloride is primarily metabolised in the liver (90%) with one of its metabolites, mono-O-desmethyltramadol (M1), being 2 to 4 times as potent as the parent compound. Tramadol Hydrochloride has a linear pharmacokinetic profile within the therapeutic dosage range. Tramadol Hydrochloride crosses the blood-brain and placental barrier. Small amounts are excreted in breast milk unchanged or as the metabolite M1. Tramadol Hydrochloride and its metabolites are excreted mainly in the urine. The elimination half-life is 5 to 7 hours, but is prolonged in impaired hepatic and renal function. Tramadol is a centrally acting analgesic which possesses opioid agonist properties.
DRP-5457.indications: Tramadol Hydrochloride is indicated for the management of moderate to moderately severe pain. DRP-5518-09.description: Each 5 mL (1 teaspoonful) of the reconstituted suspension contains: Cefixime (as Trihydrate) USP ................ 100 mg Cefixime is a third generation cephalosporin with antibacterial activity similar to penicillins, carbacephems and cephamycins. Cefixime exerts its bactericidal activity by interfering with the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall. It binds to specific penicillin-binding proteins responsible for the synthesis of peptidoglycan, a heteropolymeric structure that gives the cell wall its mechanical stability. The final stage of peptidoglycan synthesis involves completion of the cross-linking of the terminal glycine residue of the pentaglycine bridge to the fourth residue of the pentapeptide. The transpeptidase that catalyzes this step is inhibited by cephalosporins. Thus, inhibition of the transpeptidase interrupts peptidoglycan synthesis, causing formation of defective cell walls and osmotically unstable spheroplasts and lysis of the bacteria. Only 40 to 50% of an oral dose of Cefixime is absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, whether taken before or after meals, although the rate of absorption may be decreased in the presence of food. Cefixime is better absorbed from oral suspension than from tablets. Absorption is fairly slow; peak plasma concentrations of 2 to 3 micrograms/mL and 3.7 to 4.6 micrograms/mL have been reported between 2 and 6 hours after single doses of 200 and 400 mg, respectively. The plasma half-life is usually about 3 to 4 hours and may be prolonged when there is renal impairment. About 65% of Cefixime is bound to plasma proteins. Information on the distribution of Cefixime in body tissues and fluids is limited. It crosses the placenta. Relatively high concentrations may be achieved in bile and urine. About 20% of an oral dose (or 50% of an absorbed dose) is excreted unchanged in the urine within 24 hours. Up to 60% may be eliminated by non renal mechanism; there is no evidence of metabolism but some is probably excreted in the feces from bile. It is not substantially removed by dialysis.

DRP-5688.indications: Cefixime is an orally active cephalosporin antibiotic which has marked in vitro bactericidal activity against a wide variety of Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms. It is indicated for the treatment of the following acute infections when caused by susceptible micro-organisms: Upper Respiratory Tract Infections (URTI): e.g. otitis media; and other URTI where the causative organism is known or suspected to be resistant to other commonly used antibiotics, or where treatment failure may carry significant risk. Lower Respiratory Tract Infection: e.g. bronchitis. Urinary Tract Infections: e.g. cystitis, cystourethritis, uncomplicated pyelonephritis. Clinical efficacy has been demonstrated in infections caused by commonly occurring pathogens including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus pyogenes, Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, Kliebsiella species, Haemophilus influenzae (beta-lactamase positive and negative), Branhamella catarrhalis (beta-lactamase positive and negative) and Enterobacter species. Cefixime is highly stable in the presence of beta-lactamase enzymes. Most strains of enterococci (Streptococcus faecalis, group D Streptococci) and Staphylococci (including coagulase positive and negative strains and meticillin-resistant strains) are resistant to Cefixime. In addition, most strains of Pseudomonas, Bacteriodes fragalis, Listeria monocytogenes and Clostridia are resistant to Cefixime.

DRP-6376.description: Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic which was first isolated from cultures of Streptomyces Venezuelae but is now produced synthetically. It has a relatively simple structure and is a derivative of dichloroacetic acid with a nitrobenzene moiety. Chloramphenicol was the first broad-spectrum antibiotics to be discovered; it acts by interfering with bacterial protein synthesis and is mainly bacteriostatic. It is active when given by mouth and unlike most other antibiotics, it diffuses into the cerebrospinal fluid even when the meninges are not inflamed. The majority of a dose is inactivated in the liver, only a small proportion appearing unchanged in the urine.
DRP-6376.indications: Chloramphenicol is indicated for typhoid fever, bacteremia, meningitis, and other serious infections caused by microorganisms known to be sensitive to Chloramphenicol.

Its structural formula is: Pyridostigmine bromide (MUSTONE) is available in the following forms: Syrup containing 60 mg pyridostigmine bromide per teaspoonful in a vehicle containing 5% alcohol, glycerin, lactic acid, sodium benzoate, sorbitol, sucrose, FD&C Red No. 40, FD&C Blue No. 1, flavors and water. DRP-664.description: • Ambroxol hydrochloride 15 mg / 5 mL Syrup (Amectuss) is a clear, light yellow, viscous lemon flavored syrup. • Ambroxol hydrochloride 30 mg / 5 mL Syrup (Amectuss) is a clear, light, yellow, , viscous cola flavored syrup. What is in the medicine? The medicine contains ambroxol hydrochloride which is a mucolytic agent and alters the structure of mucus to decrease its viscosity there by facilitating its removal by ciliary action or expectoration. Strength of the medicine Please see formulation. What is this medicine for? This medicine is used for the treatment of respiratory disorders associated with viscid mucus. How much and how often should you use this medicine? • Ambroxol hydrochloride 15 mg / 5 mL Syrup (Amectuss) Children 6 to 12 years old - 5 mL (1 teaspoonful) 2 to 3 times daily. Children 2 to 6 years old - 2.5 mL (1/2 teaspoon) 2 to 3 times daily. Children 1 to 2 years old - 2.5 mL (1/2 teaspoon) 2 times daily. •Ambroxol hydrochloride 30 mg / 5 mL Syrup (Amectuss) Children 6 to 12 years old - 5 mL (1 teaspoonful) 2 to 3 times daily. Children 2 to 6 years old - 2.5 mL (1/2 teaspoon) 2 to 3 times daily. Children 1 to 2 years old - 2.5 mL (1/2 teaspoon) 2 times daily. Or, as prescribed by the physician. When should you not take this medicine? If you are allergic to ambroxol or any ingredient in the product. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Undesirable effects Rarely adverse gastrointestinal effects (nausea, abdominal pain) and allergic reactions (skin rash, facial swelling, severe respiration-impairment, temperature increase with fever) might be observed during treatment. What other medicines or food should be avoided while taking this medicine? Please tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking/using or have recently taken/ used any other medicines, including medicines obtained without prescription. There are no clinically significant adverse interactions with other drugs. What should you do if you miss a dose? If you miss a dose just take the next prescribed dose at the usual time. Do not double the dose. How should you keep this medicine? Store at temperatures not exceeding 30ºC. Keep away from light. Keep bottle tightly closed. AMBROXOL Hydrochloride 15 mg / 5 mL Syrup 30 mg / 5 mL Syrup Mucolytic AMECTUSS Dimensions: 216mm x 93mm Signs and symptoms of over dosage No severe poisoning symptoms have been observed. Transient agitation and diarrhea may occur. In case of significant overdose, increased salivation may occur, as well as nausea, vomiting and hypotension. A doctor should be consulted. Usually immediate intervention such as induction of vomiting and gastric lavage is unnecessary; such management can be considered in case of acute overdose. Treatment dependent on the observed symptoms of overdosage is recommended. What to do when you have taken more than the recommended dose? If you have taken more than the recommended dose, although no poisoining symptoms have been observed, consult a doctor right away. Care that should be taken when taking this medicine Do not take more than the recommended dose. Do not use after the expiry date of the label. Keep out of reach and sight of children. When should you consult a doctor? When undesirable effects occur, stop treatment and consult a doctor. DRP-7137.description: The medicine is a clear red syrup with sweet cherry flavor, aroma and taste contained in a 60 mL and 120 mL amber round bottle. What is in the medicine? Menthodex-DM contains: - Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide used as control of cough associated with common colds, influenza, allergy and other respiratory infections, inhalation of irritating substance and psychogenic cough. - Phenylpropanolamine HCI which is a decongestant. It works by constricting (shrinking) blood vessels (veins and arteries) in your body. Constriction of blood vessels in your sinuses, nose and chest allows drainage of those areas, which decreases congestion - Chlorphenamine Maleate that is an antihistamine used for the symptomatic relief of allergic conditions. Strength of the medicine: Each 5 mL contains: Sodium Citrate, USP 180 mg Dextromethorphan Hydrobromide 15 mg Phenylpropanolamine HCl . 15 mg Chlorphenamine Maleate 2m Ethyl Alcohol 0.51% What is this medicine used for? Suppresses dry cough and promotes expectoration in productive cough associated with asthma, pneumonia, bronchitis, pertussis and other respiratory diseases allergic or non-allergic in nature. Also used as antitussive, decongestant and antihistamine. How much and how often should you use this medicine? Children: 1-9 years old. 2.5 - 5 mL (1/2-1 teaspoonful) Adults. ...5 - 10 mL (1-2 teaspoonfuls) Every 4 hours or as prescribed by the physici an. When should you not take this medicine? Use with caution in patients with a history of liver disorder, bronchial asthma and cardiac disorders. Increasing dosage can lead to psychotic reactions, cardiovascular changes and precipitation of anginal attacks. Care that should be taken when taking this medicine: Antihistamines may cause drowsiness and dulling of mental alertness. Patients undergoing treatment with these drugs should not take charge of vehicles, other means of transportation or machinery where loss of attention may lead to accidents. Undesirable effects of this medicine: It appears to be rare and may include dizziness and gastrointestinal disturbances, CNS depression, drowsiness, headache, psychomotor impairment, and antimuscarinic effects such as dry mouth, thickened respiratory tract secretions, blurred vision, urinary difficulty or retention, constipation, and increased gastric reflux. It also may cause nervousness, restlessness, insomnia/sleep disturbances, feeling of uneasiness (anxiety), confusion, high blood pressure, rapid heartbeat (palpitation), chest tightness, muscle shaking (tremor), agitation, irritability, aggressiveness (particularly in young children) and nausea. What other medicine or food should be avoided while taking this medicine? _——— Dextromethorphan HBr - Amiodarone, Haloperidol, Propafenone, Quinidine, SSRI’s and Thioridazine Phenylpropanolamine HCI: - Do not take Phenylpropanolamine if you have taken a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) such as isocarboxazid, phenelzine or tranylcypromine in the last 14 days. A very dangerous drug interaction could occur, leading to serious hypertensive crisis (sudden, severe increase in blood pressure that can lead to stroke). - It may also enhance the sedative effects of Alcohol, Barbiturates, Hypnotics, Opioid Analgesics, Anxiolytic Sedatives, and Antipsychotics. - Amantadine with Phenylpropanolamine is reportedly causes severe psychosis. - Other medicines that may also interact with Phenylpropanolamine includes furazolidone; guanethidine; indomethacin; methyldopa; bromocriptine; caffeine in cola, tea, coffee, chocolate, and other products; theophylline ; tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, doxepin and nortriptyline; other commonly used tricyclic antidepressants, including amoxapine, clomipramine, desipramine, imipramine, protriptyline and trimipramine; phenothiazines such as chlorpromazine, thioridazine and prochlorperazine; and other commonly used phenothiazines, including fluphenazine, perphenazine, mesoridazine, and trifluoperazine. Chlorphenamine Maleate - may enhance the sedative effects of Alcohol, Barbiturates, Hypnotics, Opioid Analgesics, Anxiolytic, Sedative and Antipsychotics. What should you do if you miss a dose? Take the dose as soon as you remember but if the missed dose is near the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with the scheduled dosing. Do not double the dose. Signs and symptoms of overdose: Dextromethorphan HBr - excitation, confusion and respiratory depression may occur after overdosage. Phenylpropanolamine HCI - extreme tiredness, sweating, dizziness, a slow heart beat and a coma. Chlorphenamine Maleate - Ataxia, excitement, tremors, psychoses, hallucinations and convulsions; hyperpyrexia may also occur. What to do when you have taken more than the recommended dosage? If you ingested more than the recommended dose, contact the nearest hospital or your doctor immediately. How should you keep this medicine? Store at temperatures not exceeding 30°C Protect from direct sunlight. When should you consult your doctor? If symptoms persist, consult your doctor. DRP-8139.description: RiteMED® Pink, round, biconvex, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY PHARMACODYNAMICS Findings from in vitro and ex vivo of ATP production to glucose oxidation which decreases the consequences of recurrent ischemia and enhances left ventricular performance, (2) protecting endothelial function by increasing endothelial nitric synthase activity and nitric oxide availability, (3) preserving mi- tochondrial function and energy metabolism thus reducing ischemic left ventricular dysfunc- tion, (4) limiting intracellular acidosis, (5) limiting sodium and calcium accumulation, and (6) PHARMACOKINETICS Trimetazidine is rapidly absorbed from the intestinal mucosa after oral administration. In 13 healthy volunteers, the mean peak plasma trimetazidine concentration (Cmax; 53.6 mcg/L) was reached 1.8 hours after a single 20 mg (immediate release) oral dose. After twice daily administration of trimetazidine 20 mg for 15 days, Cmax (84.8 mcg/L) was reached in 1.7 hours. The area under the plasma trimetazidine concentration-time curve (AUC0-∞) was 508.9 mcg·h/L after a single 20 mg dose and 831.4 mcg·h/L after repeated administration. Steady state levels were reached within 24 hours and remained stable for the study duration. Trimetazidine is only weakly protein bound in plasma (~16%) and therefore is widely dis- tributed throughout the body. In 11 healthy volunteers, the volume of distribution (Vd) of trimetazidine was 318.6 L after a 40 mg intravenous dose. The elimination half-life of trimetazidine 20 mg is about 6 hours after single or repeated oral administration. More than 80% of an administered dose of trimetazidine is excreted in urine within 48 hours, with 62% of the drug eliminated unchanged. Eight metabolites have been detected in urine, however, little is known of their properties.

DRP-8234.description: Clear, orange syrup with orange flavor WHAT IS IN THE MEDICINE? Vitamin C, a water-soluble vitamin, is essential for the synthesis of collagen and intercellular material. Zinc is needed for the proper growth and maintenance of the human body. It is needed for the immune function, wound healing, blood clotting, thyroid function, and much more. STRENGTH OF THE MEDICINE Please see formulation WHAT IS THIS MEDICINE USED FOR? Sodium ascorbate used to increase body resistance against stress, colds and other infections. Also for the prevention and treatment of scurvy. Zinc is for boosting the immune system, treating the common cold and preventing lower respiratory infections. HOW MUCH AND HOW OFTEN SHOULD YOU USE THIS MEDICINE? Children 9-13 yrs. old: 5-10 mL (1-2 teaspoonful) 4-8 years old: 5 mL (1 teaspoonful) 1-3 years old: 2.5 mL (½ teaspoonful) To be taken once daily for supplementation. Twice or thrice a daily for therapeutic use. Or as prescribed by the physician. WHEN SHOULD YOU NOT TAKE THIS MEDICINE? If you are allergic to any ingredients. CARE THAT SHOULD BE TAKEN WHEN TAKING THIS MEDICINE? Large doses may result in hyperoxaluria and the formation of renal calcium oxalate calculi and sodium ascorbate should therefore be given with care to patients with hyperoxaluria. Infants and children: Zinc is possibly unsafe when used in high doses. This product contains FD & C #5 (Tartrazine) which may cause allergic reactions including bronchial asthma in certain susceptible persons. UNDESIRABLE EFFECTS OF THIS MEDICINE? Large doses of sodium ascorbate have resulted in haemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. WHAT OTHER MEDICINE OR FOOD SHOULD BE AVOIDED WHILE TAKING THIS MEDICINE? Sodium Ascorbate may increase the absorption of iron in iron-deficiency states. Taking zinc along with some antibiotics (Quinolones) might decrease the effectiveness of some antibiotics. DRP-8718-01.description: This product is a light brown to brown powder encapsulated in an empty gelatin capsule size #0 with scarlet opaque cap and scarlet opaque body. WHAT IS IN THE PRODUCT AND WHAT IS IT USED FOR? The product contains Vitamin B 1, Vitamin B2, Vitamin B3, Folic Acid, Cyanocobalamin and Iron. This product is used for treatment and prevention of vitamins B 1, B 2, B 3, B 12, folate and iron deficiencies. STRENGTH OF THE PRODUCT Each capsule contains: Thiamine Mononitrate (Vitamin B 1), USP……………………...............…….....10 mg Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)…………………………………………………..................5 mg Nicotinamide (Vitamin B3)……………………………………………..................20 mg Folic Acid (Vitamin B9)………….……………………………………….….......800 mcg Cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12)…………………………………........................25 mcg Iron (as Ferrous Fumarate)...………………………………………....................164 mg HOW MUCH AND HOW OFTEN SHOULD YOU USE THIS PRODUCT? Adults: 1 capsule daily or as prescribed by a physician. WHEN SHOULD YOU NOT TAKE THE PRODUCT? If you are allergic to any component of the product. CARE THAT SHOULD BE TAKEN WHEN TAKING THE PRODUCT • Do not take more than the recommended dose. • Do not use after the expiry date on the label. UNDESIRABLE EFFECTS • Gastrointestinal side effects such as nausea, vomiting, bloating, diarrhea, constipation and upper abdominal discomfort are seen with high iron doses. • Stools may appear darker in color. WHAT OTHER MEDICINES OR FOOD SHOULD BE AVOIDED WHILE TAKING THE PRODUCT? • Do not use together with antacids and tetracyclines. • Do not use together with chloramphenicol. It is also important that you tell your doctor if you are taking, or have recently taken, any other medicines even those not prescribed. For suspected adverse drug reaction, report to the FDA: www.fda.gov.ph. Seek medical attention immediately at the first sign of any adverse drug reaction. WHAT SHOULD YOU DO IF YOU MISS A DOSE? If you have missed a dose just give the next dose and the subsequent doses as the usually recommended schedule, ex. Once a day. Do not double the dose unless prescribed by a physician. SIGNS AND SYMPTOMS OF OVERDOSE • Vitamin B 1 - Adults who overdose on Vitamin B 1 might suffer from chills, swelling, nervousness, increased heart rate and allergies. • Vitamin B2 - Side effects from taking more than 10 mg per day of Riboflavin include sun-induced eye damage, itching or numbing sensations, and orange-tinted urine. • Vitamin B3 - A Vitamin B3 overdose can cause liver damage and abnormal gastric ulceration. • Vitamin B9 - Extremely large doses of folic acid (exceeding 15,000 micrograms) have been known to cause digestive problems, insomnia, skin reactions and seizures. • Vitamin B 12 - A Vitamin B 12 overdose can lead to itchiness on different body parts and numbness, improper heart functioning, giddiness and regular headaches. • Iron - Doses of more than 25 mg a day can cause fatigue, weight loss, constipation, headache, zinc deficiencies, copper deficiencies, and damage to the pancreas, liver and heart muscle. WHAT TO DO WHEN YOU HAVE MORE THAN THE RECOMMENDED DOSE? If you have more than the recommended dose, consult a doctor or contact a poison center right away. HOW SHOULD YOU KEEP THE PRODUCT? • Keep the product out of reach and sight of children. • Store at temperatures not exceeding 30ºC. WHEN SHOULD YOU CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR? If any undesirable effect occurs.

DRP-8914.indications: Distribution: The steady-state volume of distribution of Valsartan after intravenous administration is about 17 liters indicating that Valsartan is not distributed into tissues extensively. Valsartan is highly bound to serum proteins (94-97%), mainly serum albumin. Biotransformation: Valsartan is not transformed to a high extent as only about 20% of dose is recovered as metabolites. A hydroxy metabolite has been identified in plasma at low concentrations (less than 10% of the Valsartan AUC). This metabolite is pharmacologically inactive. Valsartan/Amlodipine: Following oral administration of Amlodipine + Valsartan peak plasma concentrations of Amlodipine + Valsartan are reached in 3 and 6-8 hours, respectively. The rate and extent of absorption of Amlodipine + Valsartan are equivalent to the bioavailability of Valsartan and amlodipine when administered as individual tablets. Special populations: Geriatric patients: The time to reach peak plasma concentrations of amlodipine is similar in elderly and younger subjects. Amlodipine clearance tends to be decreased with resulting increases in AUC and elimination half-life in elderly patients. Hepatic impairment: Patients with hepatic impairment have decreased clearance of Amlodipine with resulting increase in AUC of approximately 40-60%. On average, in patients with mild to moderate chronic liver disease exposure (measured by AUC values) to Valsartan is twice that found in healthy volunteers (matched by age, sex and weight). Care should be exercised in patients with liver disease. Systemic exposure to Valsartan is slightly elevated in the elderly as compared to the young, but this has not been shown to have any clinical significance.
